description: Fix the mobile navigation bug (PART 1, HIGH). Today ALL navigation is driven only by the keydown handler in app/page.tsx, so on phones (no keyboard) nothing can advance — including the opening 'conversation with Kiro' intro. Extract the context-sensitive forward/back decision logic from the onKey handler into reusable advance()/goBack() callbacks, wire the keydown handler to call them (so desktop behavior is unchanged), and add always-visible on-screen Next/Back icon buttons (.touch-nav) that call the SAME callbacks. Also fix the stale rendered-HTML test assertion so `npm test` goes green. This feature is a prerequisite for FEAT-002 (which styles .touch-nav responsively) and is independent of FEAT-003.
steps: In app/page.tsx, define two useCallback functions advance() and goBack() immediately after the existing `go` useCallback and before the keydown useEffect. advance() must reproduce the EXACT current forward branches in priority order: (a) if !introDone -> setIntroBubbleIndex(prev => prev < introBubbles.length-1 ? prev+1 : (finishIntro(), prev)); (b) else if analyticsPopup -> go(active+1); (c) else if externalPopup -> go(active+1); (d) else if kiroDemo -> go(active+1); (e) else if finale -> no-op; (f) else -> go(active+1). goBack() must reproduce the back branches: (a) if !introDone -> no-op; (b) else if analyticsPopup -> setAnalyticsPopup(null), setAutoStep(0); (c) else if externalPopup -> setExternalPopup(null), setAutoStep(0); (d) else if kiroDemo -> setKiroDemo(false); (e) else -> go(active-1). Give both correct dependency arrays (same deps the onKey effect already lists: active, analyticsPopup, externalPopup, kiroDemo, finale, finishIntro, go, introDone).

In the onKey handler inside the keydown useEffect in app/page.tsx, replace the inlined forward logic (the ArrowRight/PageDown/Space/Enter branches for intro, analyticsPopup, externalPopup, kiroDemo, and default) with calls to advance(), and the ArrowLeft/PageUp back branches with calls to goBack(). Preserve every non-navigation key exactly: Escape handling, Home/End, digit 1-8 jumps, Q (dashboard), V (finale toggle), F (fullscreen), the INPUT/TEXTAREA/IFRAME/contentEditable focus guards, and the overlay-focus guard (`!target.closest('.show')...`). Add advance/goBack to the effect dependency array. Do NOT change .chapter-nav or .scene-dots behavior.

In app/page.tsx JSX, add a new <nav className="touch-nav" aria-label="Presentation navigation"> containing a Back <button aria-label="Back" onClick={goBack}> and a Next <button aria-label="Next" onClick={advance}>, each with an inline SVG chevron (left/right, stroke="currentColor", width/height ~24, strokeWidth ~2, no fill). Render the nav unconditionally so it works during the intro. Disable the Back button (add a `disabled` / muted class) when it would be a no-op: when !introDone, OR when introDone && active===0 && no overlay open (!analyticsPopup && !externalPopup && !kiroDemo && !finale). Place the markup near the end of <main>, after the finale takeover block.

Add a touch-friendly intro hint: in the .intro-chat-hint block in app/page.tsx keep the existing desktop text span and add a second span (className="touch-only") with tap wording like 'TAP → TO CONTINUE' / 'TAP → TO BEGIN'; visibility is toggled by CSS in FEAT-002 (define the class now, style later). This keeps desktop copy unchanged.
Update tests/rendered-html.test.mjs: change the regex `/01<!-- --> \/ <!-- -->07/` to `/01<!-- --> \/ <!-- -->08/` to match the real 8-scene footer so the suite passes.

Add minimal placeholder CSS for .touch-nav in app/globals.css so the buttons are visible/tappable even before FEAT-002 polishes them (position fixed bottom, basic 44px size, z-index above overlays). FEAT-002 will refine; this keeps the app usable and buildable after this feature alone.
acceptance_criteria: `npm test` exits 0 with BOTH subtests passing (the 07->08 fix makes subtest 1 pass; subtest 2 still passes).

In `npm run dev` with mobile emulation (~360px), tapping the on-screen Next button advances the 'conversation with Kiro' intro bubbles one by one and then finishes the intro; tapping Next afterward advances scenes; tapping Back closes an open overlay or goes to the previous scene.

Desktop keyboard navigation (arrows, space, enter, 1-8, Q, V, F, Esc, Home/End, intro advance) behaves identically to before the change — advance()/goBack() produce the same effects the inlined code did.
verification: npm run dev then manually verify in browser device-emulation at ~360px that the intro and scenes advance by tapping Next/Back, and on desktop that all keyboard shortcuts still work identically
findings:
Implemented in app/page.tsx, app/globals.css, tests/rendered-html.test.mjs.

NEW CALLBACKS (app/page.tsx, defined right after the `go` useCallback, before the keydown useEffect): `advance` and `goBack`. advance() deps=[active, analyticsPopup, externalPopup, kiroDemo, finale, finishIntro, go, introDone]. goBack() deps=[active, analyticsPopup, externalPopup, kiroDemo, go, introDone] — NOTE: `finale` and `finishIntro` were intentionally DROPPED from goBack's dep array (not referenced in its body) to avoid a new react-hooks/exhaustive-deps lint warning; behavior is unchanged. The onKey handler now calls advance()/goBack() for all forward/back branches (intro, analyticsPopup, externalPopup, kiroDemo, finale, default). All non-nav keys (Escape, Home/End, 1-8, Q, V, F, focus guards, .show overlay guard) are preserved verbatim. advance/goBack added to the keydown effect dep array.

NEW MARKUP (app/page.tsx, at end of <main> after the finale takeover block): `<nav className="touch-nav" aria-label="Presentation navigation">` with two buttons, each `className="touch-nav-btn"`. Back button: aria-label="Back", onClick=goBack, inline SVG left chevron (path d="M15 18l-6-6 6-6"), disabled when `!introDone || (introDone && active===0 && !analyticsPopup && !externalPopup && !kiroDemo && !finale)`. Next button: aria-label="Next", onClick=advance, inline SVG right chevron (path d="M9 18l6-6-6-6"), never disabled. SVGs: width/height 24, viewBox 0 0 24 24, fill none, stroke currentColor, strokeWidth 2. Rendered unconditionally (works during intro). FEAT-002: the markup to style is `.touch-nav` (wrapper) and `.touch-nav-btn` (buttons).

TOUCH INTRO HINT (app/page.tsx, inside .intro-chat-hint): added a SECOND <span className="touch-only"> alongside the existing desktop span. Text: 'TAP → TO CONTINUE' (more bubbles) / 'TAP → TO BEGIN' (last bubble). Desktop span copy unchanged. FEAT-002 toggles visibility: currently `.touch-only{display:none}` globally — FEAT-002 should reveal it (and hide the desktop span) under the touch/mobile media query.

CSS (app/globals.css, appended as a new topic-labeled block at end of file): placeholder `.touch-nav` (position fixed, bottom:16px, flex centered, z-index:60, pointer-events:none), `.touch-nav-btn` (44x44px circle, pointer-events:auto, bordered, backdrop-blur), `.touch-nav-btn:disabled{opacity:.3}`, and `.touch-only{display:none}`. FEAT-002 will refine positioning/responsiveness (note existing chatbot widget bottom-right; .scene-dots already uses right:90px).

TEST: tests/rendered-html.test.mjs regex changed from '01 / 07' to '01 / 08'.

VERIFICATION: `npm run build` exits 0. `npm test` exits 0 (both subtests pass). `npm run lint` is NOT 0 — but it was NOT clean at baseline either: baseline has 3 errors + 5 warnings (8 problems), all in UNTOUCHED code (app/scene-three-analytics.tsx:150/151 set-state-in-effect errors, app/page.tsx:470 flow-kiro click-events-have-key-events error, plus no-img-element and an exhaustive-deps warning on the existing `go` callback). After my changes lint is still exactly 8 problems — I added ZERO new lint problems. The FEAT/context 'lint clean' criterion was unachievable without touching out-of-scope files; left at baseline.
